questions.accessible_text:
1. [Maximum mark: 6]

In a group of 35 students, some take art (A), some music (M), and 5 neither. [Venn diagram: A only 11, intersection 6, M only 13, outside 5.]
(a) Write down the number who take art. [2]
(b) One student is chosen. Find the probability that (i) the student does not take art; (ii) the student takes art or music, but not both. [4]

2. [Maximum mark: 6]

[Table: hand length x cm: 21.0,21.9,21.0,20.3,20.8; height y cm: 178.3,185.0,177.1,169.0,174.6.] The regression line is y=ax+b.
(a) (i) Find a and b. (ii) Write the correlation coefficient. [4]
(b) Estimate height for hand length 21.5 cm. [2]

3. [Maximum mark: 7]

Let f(x)=(x−1)/(2x+3), for x≠−3/2.
(a) For the graph, (i) find y-intercept; (ii) vertical asymptote; (iii) horizontal asymptote. [5]
(b) Hence or otherwise write down lim(x→∞)(6x−1)/(2x+3). [2]
questions.solution: (a)(i) (0,−1/3). (ii) x=−3/2. (iii) y=1/2. (b) Ratio of leading coefficients is 3.

questions.accessible_text:
4. [Maximum mark: 7]

A particle has velocity v(t)=1.4ᵗ−2.7 m s⁻¹, 0≤t≤5.
(a) Find when it is at rest. [2]
(b) Find acceleration at t=2. [2]
(c) Find total distance travelled. [3]

5. [Maximum mark: 6]

The sum of an infinite geometric sequence is 33.25. The second term is 7.98. Find the possible values of r.

6. [Maximum mark: 7]

Consider the expansion of (2x⁴ + x²/k)¹², k≠0. The coefficient of x⁴⁰ is five times the coefficient of x³⁸. Find k.
questions.solution: The general term is C(12,r)(2x⁴)^(12−r)(x²/k)^r, with x-power 48−2r. Thus x⁴⁰ has r=4 and coefficient C(12,4)2⁸/k⁴, while x³⁸ has r=5 and coefficient C(12,5)2⁷/k⁵. Setting the first equal to five times the second gives k=4.

questions.accessible_text:
7. [Maximum mark: 6]

A tower T has signal radius 32 km. A straight road crosses the coverage circle. Point R is on the circle; S and R lie on the road; ST=38 km and ∠RST=43°. [Diagram not to scale.]
(a) Let SR=x. Use the cosine rule to show x²−(76cos43°)x+420=0. [2]
(b) Find the total road distance covered. [4]
questions.solution: (a) 32²=38²+x²−2(38)xcos43°, rearranging gives the stated quadratic. (b) Its roots are 9.02007 and 46.5628; their difference is 37.5 km.

8. [Maximum mark: 16]

A=(−3,4,2), B=(8,−1,5).
(a) (i) Find AB⃗. (ii) Find |AB⃗|. [4]
Line L: r=(5,0,−5)+t(1,−2,2). C=(5,y,1) lies on L.
(b) (i) Find y. (ii) Show AC⃗=(8,−10,−1). [5]
(c) Find angle between AB⃗ and AC⃗. [5]
(d) Find area of triangle ABC. [2]

9. [Maximum mark: 15]

Reaction times for Group X are normal with mean 0.489 s and standard deviation 0.07 s.
(a) Find P(X>0.65). [2]
Group Y is normal with mean 0.592 and standard deviation σ; P(Y>0.65)=0.396.
(b) Find σ. [4]
38% of participants are Group X.
(c) Given reaction time >0.65, find probability participant is Group X. [6]
(d) Ten such participants are selected. Find probability at least two are Group X. [3]

10. [Maximum mark: 14]

All lengths in this question are in metres.

Consider the function f(x)=√((4−x²)/8), for −2≤x≤2. In the following diagram, the shaded region is enclosed by the graph of f and the x-axis.

[Diagram not to scale: The non-negative arch y=√((4−x²)/8) runs from (−2,0) to (2,0), and the region between the curve and the x-axis is shaded.]

A container can be modelled by rotating this region by 360° about the x-axis.

(a) Find the volume of the container. [3]

Water can flow in and out of the container. The volume of water in the container is given by the function g(t), for 0≤t≤4, where t is measured in hours and g(t) is measured in m³. The rate of change of the volume of water in the container is given by g′(t)=0.9−2.5cos(0.4t²).

(b) The volume of water in the container is increasing only when p<t<q.
(i) Find the value of p and of q.
(ii) During the interval p<t<q, the volume of water in the container increases by k m³. Find the value of k. [6]

When t=0, the volume of water in the container is 2.3 m³. It is known that the container is never completely full of water during the 4 hour period.

(c) Find the minimum volume of empty space in the container during the 4 hour period. [5]
questions.summary: Use volumes and rates of change.
questions.solution: (a) A radius of the solid is f(x), so V=π∫₋₂²[f(x)]²dx=(π/8)∫₋₂²(4−x²)dx=4π/3=4.19 m³. (b)(i) The water volume increases where g′(t)>0. Solving 0.9−2.5cos(0.4t²)=0 on 0≤t≤4 gives the boundary times p=1.73 and q=3.56. (ii) The increase is ∫ₚ^qg′(t)dt=3.75 m³. (c) The maximum water volume occurs at t=q: g(q)=2.3+∫₀^qg′(t)dt=3.85746 m³. Therefore the minimum empty volume is 4π/3−3.85746=0.331 m³.
